chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who arrives at the Sacred Monument (Mash'ar al-Haram), and upon it are five from the people, so he has accomplished the Hajj.

key_terms.الْمَشْعَرَ الْحَرَامَ: The Sacred Monument (referring to Mash'ar al-Haram)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of people required at the Sacred Monument to validate the Hajj according to this narration?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific condition for the validity of Hajj, emphasizing the communal aspect of the ritual by requiring the presence of at least five pilgrims at Mash'ar al-Haram. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on the collective performance of rites, distinguishing it from mere individual presence, and underscores the significance of Mash'ar al-Haram as a critical locus for Hajj completion. The chain of transmission through prominent figures like Ibn Abi Umayr and Hisham ibn al-Hakam attests to its reliability within the Usuli tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who arrives at the Sacred Monuments, and upon it are (at least) five from the people (remaining), so he has accomplished the Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who attends al-Mash‘ar al-Haram (the sacred area) when five people are still there, he is considered, as having attended al-Hajj. ‘“
